title: Staggered Anchor Validation and Cost-Fingerprint Pipeline
creator: Katherine Li
description: Problem: Model performance profiles (latency, throughput, normalized cost) go stale as models, kernels, or infra change. Current publish flow is manual and relies on single-stage verification that produces brittle pins and frequent rollbacks. Goal: build an automated, staggered validation pipeline that generates a signed "cost fingerprint" and stability score for each model version, supports safe pin publish/rollforward, and provides transparent artifacts for QA and SRE.
background: We maintain Redwood-verified performance profiles for every model + variant combination. Profiles are used for routing, pricing, and canary logic. Past incidents: two rollouts that used stale profiles and caused higher than expected latency and cost spikes. Engineering has instrumented additional telemetry (p50/p95 latency per-token, throughput by batch-size, KV cache hit ratios, kernel selection histogram). Product needs a reproducible publish pipeline that codifies sampling, statistical thresholds, and rollback hooks so PM/Eng/Runbook owners can trust published pins.
objectives: Automate sampling and validation for new model versions and runtime builds
Compute a compact cost-fingerprint artifact (median latency, p95 latency, throughput, normalized $/1M tokens, variance metrics) and a stability score
Stage validation in three staggered gates: synthetic lab, shadow traffic, and low-traffic canary, with automated fail/rollback criteria
Publish signed profile manifest to the git-backed registry and trigger downstream routing/publish webhooks
Expose status & diffs in Console with clear rollback actions and root-cause pointers
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline runs end-to-end for a test model version and produces a signed manifest committed to the profile registry
Stability score computed and stored; scores < 0.7 block automatic publish
Console shows a per-model diff (latency/throughput/cost) and highlights regressions beyond configured thresholds
A canary that fails automated thresholds triggers an automatic rollback and a GitHub issue template is created
Runbook updated with playbook steps and SLOs for manual override
Telemetry contract validated: p50, p95, throughput, tokens-per-second, and cost-per-1M emitted and visible on dashboard
implementation_outline: Lab stage: run deterministic sample harness (10k requests across target seq lengths & batch sizes) and compute fingerprint
Shadow stage: mirror 1% of production traffic for 24h; compute drift metrics vs anchor
Canary stage: route 0.1% live traffic for 6h with strict thresholds and emergency cutoff
Signature: sign JSON manifest with CI key and push to git-backed registry; manifest includes version, model hash, kernel candidates, cost-fingerprint, stability score, and provenance links
Console integration: diff UI, signed-manifest viewer, and one-click rollback
Automation: a reconciliation job that re-evaluates anchors weekly and surfaces candidates for steward review
technical_decisions: Use stratified sampling by sequence length and prompt shape to avoid bias toward short-context benchmarks
Normalize cost to a canonical currency unit (USD / 1M tokens) using current infra pricing and amortized GPU utilization
Compute stability score as a weighted composite: latency stability (40%), throughput stability (30%), cost variance (20%), unseen regression flags (10%)
Store manifests in existing profiles git repo using signed commit flow; rollback is a revert commit and webhook to runtime config
Shadow traffic will be rate-limited and scrubbed to avoid PII leakage; metrics aggregation will use existing telemetry paths
risks: Overfitting to synthetic lab samples producing optimistic fingerprints
False positives triggering rollbacks due to transient infra noise
Complexity of signature/key management for automated signing
Increased infra load during shadow/canary stages if sampling not throttled
mitigations: Include production-like prompt mixes in sampling harness and rotate seed prompts weekly
Use rolling-window baseline and require persistent deviations over multiple windows before automatic rollback
Integrate signing key management with KMS and require CI-level approval for signing
Autoscale sample runners and cap shadow traffic to strict percentiles (1% max)
